newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Sydney Casino records March qtr loss.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Sydney Casino records March qtr loss.

text.p: Sydney Harbour Casino Ltd said on Tuesday it recorded a loss of A$600,000 for the three months to March 31 compared with a profit of A$600,000 for the year earlier.

Sydney Harbour Casino said in a statement accompanying its March quarter report that construction of the permanent casino was on schedule and on budget. The A$876 million casino complex is due to open in December this year.

Warburton said Sydney Harbour Casino incurred total abnormal costs of A$19.2 million during the March quater, due mainly to pre-opening costs and interest payments for the permanent casino. The combined result of the temporary casino resulted in a loss after abnormal items and tax of A$600,000.

"Once again we have taken the view that we should meet interest and pre-opening costs relating to the permanent casino as they are incurred rather than capitalising these expenses," chairman Dick Warburton said.
"If we had opted to defer these payments until after the permanent casino opens we would have recorded an operating profit before tax of A$13 million for the March quarter.
"So while our policy is restricting profits in the short term, we will be in a very sound position when the casino opens in December this year," he said.
The company said the casino had attracted more than 15,000 visitors a day during the period, with weekend attendances regularly exceeding 20,000 -- the best figures yet recorded.

"That is a remarkable performance and it reflects the sharper focus on marketing initiatives, improved access facilities and the very popular entertainment package we have been offering at the casino in recent months," Warburton said.
He said the casino had provided more than 300,000 meals during the first quarter, about 57,000 more than in the same period last year.
"In other words there has been a surge in patronage in all areas of our operations, from food and beverage and entertainment to gaming," he added.
He said highlights of the quarter included:
-- Net revenue A$103 million, up 11 percent from year ago
-- Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation up 9.2 percent to A$26 million
-- Operating profit before abnormal items up nearly 10 percent to A$18.6 million

Warburton said the overriding priority for 1997 remained the completion and move to the permanent casino and hotel facility to accomodate inherent demand that could not be fully met by the temporary facility.
Preparations would be stepped up in the coming months and the number of employees would almost double to 5,000 by the end of the year," he said.
